content:
The Honest Trader

Alhaji Musa was a trader in the central market of Kano. He sold grains, and his customers trusted him because he never cheated them. One day, a woman bought a bag of rice from him and paid with a large sum of money. When she left, Musa discovered that she had overpaid by five thousand naira. His assistant advised him to keep the money, saying the woman would never know. But Musa shook his head. He closed his shop early, found the woman's house, and returned the money to her. The woman was surprised and grateful. She told her neighbours about Musa's honesty, and from that day, more people came to buy from him. His business grew, not because he was clever with money, but because he was honest.

content:
The Village School

When Amina was a little girl, there was no school in her village. The nearest school was in a town six kilometres away, and many children could not walk that far every day. Amina's father was a farmer, and he wanted his daughter to learn to read and write. Every morning, he woke her before dawn, and they walked together to the town. Sometimes the road was muddy, and sometimes the sun was very hot, but Amina never complained. She loved her lessons, especially reading. Years later, Amina became a teacher. She returned to her village and, with the help of the community, built a small school. Today, the children of the village no longer walk six kilometres to learn. They study in their own village, and Amina is their teacher.
